lines.text: Day nine. A hundred and eighty feet above the ocean. The safest building on Earth.
lines.cap:
DAY 9. 180 FEET UP. THE
SAFEST BUILDING ON EARTH.

lines.text: And it's been running without a crew for forty days.
lines.cap:
IT'S RUN WITHOUT A CREW
FOR FORTY DAYS.

lines.text: One helideck. One ladder. They can't swim, and they can't climb.
lines.cap:
ONE HELIDECK. ONE LADDER.
THEY CAN'T SWIM OR CLIMB.

lines.text: Rule one. Raise the boat-landing ladder.
You winch it up. Now there is no way up at all.
lines.cap:
YOU WINCH IT UP.
NOW THERE IS NO WAY UP.

lines.text: Radio. Recovery in two days. Hold at Rig Bravo. Own water. Own power. Sixty bunks.
lines.cap:
RADIO: HOLD AT RIG BRAVO.
OWN WATER. OWN POWER.

lines.text: Rule two. Keep the helideck lights off.
You kill the lights. From the air, from the sea, the rig is gone.
lines.cap:
YOU KILL THE LIGHTS.
THE RIG IS GONE.

lines.text: Sixty bunks. A year of food. Zero ways up.
lines.cap:
60 BUNKS. A YEAR OF FOOD.
ZERO WAYS UP.

lines.text: Rule three. Read the log before you touch anything.
lines.cap:
RULE 3. READ THE LOG BEFORE
YOU TOUCH ANYTHING.

lines.text: So you touch nothing. You find the control room. You find the log.
Six twenty PM. Thirty-nine days of entries. Every one routine.
lines.cap:
6:20 PM. 39 DAYS OF ENTRIES.
EVERY ONE ROUTINE.

lines.text: Forty people. Zero ways up. And it came by radio.
lines.cap:
40 PEOPLE. ZERO WAYS UP.
AND IT CAME BY RADIO.

lines.text: Then the thing that ends the night. The winter fuel isn't here.
It's four hundred miles further south. On the ice.
Do you read the rest of the log?
